0.long_answer: The total incidence of childhood leukemia refers to the overall number of new cases rather than just a rate. According to the available global burden studies, one report estimated that in 2020 there were approximately 67,008 new cases of childhood leukemia worldwide. Although different studies may report slightly varied numbers (for instance, another study noted around 58,785 cases in 2021), the figure of about 67,008 new cases is a commonly cited estimate for the total incidence in a given year.

1.long_answer: T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL/LBL) is recognized as a subset of childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia cases. Epidemiological data suggest that it accounts for approximately 15% of childhood ALL cases, with some reports indicating a range from 10% to 25% among newly diagnosed cases. This indicates that while T-ALL/LBL is less common compared to other subtypes, it still represents a significant portion of pediatric leukemia diagnoses.
